title.zh: 卷六十 列傳第二十 范泰 王准之 王韶之 荀伯子
title.en: Volume 60 Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Zhunzhi, Xun Bozi
title.raw: 卷六十 列傳第二十 范泰 王准之 王韶之 荀伯子 Volume 60 Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Zhunzhi, Xun Bozi

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十 范泰王淮之王韶之荀伯子

translations.literal: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Huaizhi, Wang Shaozhi, Xun Bozi
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Huaizhi, Wang Shaozhi, and Xun Bozi

sentences.zh: 范泰，字伯倫，順陽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Fan Tai, courtesy name Bolun, was a man of Shanyin in Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tai, whose courtesy name was Bolun, came from Shanyin in Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 祖汪，晉安北將軍、徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wang was Jin General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of the two provinces Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang had served as Jin's General Who Pacifies the North and as inspector of Xu and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 父寧，豫章太守。

translations.literal: His father Ning was Prefect of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning had been prefect of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 泰初為太學博士，衛將軍謝安、驃騎將軍會稽王道子二府參軍。

translations.literal: Tai was at first an erudite of the Imperial Academy and a staff officer in the two offices of General-in-Chief Xie An and Rapid Cavalry General the Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Tai began as an erudite at the Imperial Academy and then served as a staff officer under both General-in-Chief Xie An and Rapid Cavalry General Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史王忱，泰外弟也，請為天門太守。

translations.literal: Wang Chen, Inspector of Jing Province, was Tai's cousin on his mother's side; he requested him as Administrator of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, the inspector of Jing Province and Tai's cousin on his mother's side, asked that Tai be appointed administrator of Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 忱嗜酒，醉輒累旬，及醒，則儼然端肅。

translations.literal: Chen was addicted to wine; when drunk he would remain so for many days on end, yet when he sobered he would be stern and dignified as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was a heavy drinker who could stay drunk for weeks at a stretch, yet once sober he would again be perfectly composed and dignified.

sentences.zh: 泰謂忱曰：「酒雖會性，亦所以傷生。

translations.literal: Tai said to Chen: "Though wine suits one's nature, it is also what harms life.
translations.idiomatic: Tai told Chen, "Wine may suit one's temperament, but it also ruins one's health.

sentences.zh: 游處以來，常欲有以相戒，當卿沈湎，措言莫由，及今之遇，又無假陳說。」

translations.literal: Since we have been together I have often wished to offer some warning; when you were sunk in drink there was no way to put words to it, and on this present meeting there is again no occasion to set forth my views."
translations.idiomatic: Ever since we have kept company I have wanted to warn you, but while you were lost in drink there was no way to speak, and now that we meet again there is still no proper moment to lay out what I mean."

sentences.zh: 忱嗟歎久之，曰：「見規者眾矣，未有若此者也。」

translations.literal: Chen sighed for a long while and said: "Many have admonished me, but none like this."
translations.idiomatic: Chen sighed at length and said, "Many people have tried to correct me, but never like this."

sentences.zh: 或問忱曰：「范泰何如謝邈？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Chen: "How does Fan Tai compare with Xie Miao?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Chen, "How does Fan Tai compare with Xie Miao?"

sentences.zh: 忱曰：「茂度慢。」

translations.literal: Chen said: "Maodu is slow."
translations.idiomatic: Chen replied, "Maodu is sluggish."

sentences.zh: 又問：「何如殷覬？」

translations.literal: He was asked again: "How does he compare with Yin Kai?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "What about Yin Kai?"

sentences.zh: 忱曰：「伯通易。」

translations.literal: Chen said: "Botong is easy."
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "Botong is easier to deal with."

sentences.zh: 忱常有意立功，謂泰曰：「今城池既立，軍甲亦充，將欲掃除中原，以申宿昔之志。

translations.literal: Chen often wished to achieve merit and said to Tai: "Now that the walls and defenses are set up and arms and armor are ample, I intend to sweep clean the Central Plains and fulfill my long-cherished resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Chen often wanted to win distinction in battle and told Tai, "Our fortifications are in place and our arms are ready; I mean to drive the enemy from the Central Plains and at last fulfill the ambition I have nursed for years.

sentences.zh: 伯通意銳，當令擁戈前驅。

translations.literal: Botong's will is keen; he should be made to take spear in hand and lead the van.
translations.idiomatic: Botong is eager for action and should lead the advance with weapons in hand.

sentences.zh: 以君持重，欲相委留事，何如？」

translations.literal: Because you are steady and weighty, I wish to entrust the rear affairs to you—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Because you are steady and reliable, I would like to leave the rear administration to you—what do you say?"

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「百年逋寇，前賢挫屈者多矣。

translations.literal: Tai said: "For a hundred years the fugitive enemy has caused many former worthies to be broken and bent.
translations.idiomatic: Tai replied, "This enemy has eluded us for a century, and many eminent men before us have been defeated in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 功名雖貴，鄙生所不敢謀。」

translations.literal: Though fame and merit are precious, this humble man does not dare to scheme for them."
translations.idiomatic: Fame and achievement are splendid things, but I am too mean a man to dare plot for them."

sentences.zh: 會忱病卒。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Chen fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chen fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 召泰為驃騎諮議參軍，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Tai was summoned as Adviser Staff Officer to the Rapid Cavalry General and promoted to Gentleman Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was recalled to serve as an advising staff officer to the Rapid Cavalry General and was then promoted to gentleman attendant of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時會稽王世子元顯專權，內外百官請假，不復表聞，唯籤元顯而已。

translations.literal: At that time the Heir Apparent of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, held sole power; officials within and without, when requesting leave, no longer reported by memorial but only submitted notes to Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuanxian, heir apparent of Kuaiji, held all real power; officials throughout the government, when asking for leave, no longer sent memorials to the throne but only filed slips with Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 泰建言以為非宜，元顯不納。

translations.literal: Tai submitted a proposal that this was not proper; Yuanxian did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Tai submitted a memorial arguing that this was improper, but Yuanxian ignored it.

sentences.zh: 父憂去職，襲爵陽遂鄉侯。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his father's mourning and inherited the title Marquis of Yangsui Township.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on his father's death and inherited the title Marquis of Yangsui township.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔晉，使御史中丞祖台之奏泰及前司徒左長史王準之、輔國將軍司馬珣之竝居喪無禮，泰坐廢徙丹徒。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted Jin, he had the Censor Grandee Zu Taizhi memorialize that Tai, together with the former Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Wang Zhunzhi and the Assisting-State General Sima Xunzhi, had all been without proper observance during mourning; Tai was punished by dismissal and banishment to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan dominated the Jin court, he had Censor-in-Chief Zu Taizhi accuse Tai, together with the former left chief clerk of the Ministry of Education Wang Zhunzhi and Assisting-State General Sima Xunzhi, of failing to observe mourning rites properly; Tai was stripped of office and exiled to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，國子博士。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, he became an erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyalist armies rose against Huan Xuan, he was appointed an erudite at the National University.

sentences.zh: 司馬休之為冠軍將軍、荊州刺史，以泰為長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi was made Champion General and Inspector of Jing Province and appointed Tai Chief Clerk and Administrator of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xiuzhi became Champion General and inspector of Jing Province, he made Tai his chief clerk and administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 又除長沙相，散騎常侍，竝不拜。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Chancellor of Changsha and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, but he accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: He was also offered the posts of chancellor of Changsha and regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, but declined both.

sentences.zh: 入為黃門郎，御史中丞。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as a gentleman of the Yellow Gates and then as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 坐議殷祠事謬，白衣領職。

translations.literal: Because of an error in deliberation over the Yin ancestral sacrifices, he served in office as a commoner in white.
translations.idiomatic: He was faulted for a mistake in deliberations over the Yin ancestral sacrifices and continued to hold office only as a commoner out of mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 出為東陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 盧循之難，泰預發兵千人，開倉給稟，高祖加泰振武將軍。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of Lu Xun, Tai beforehand raised a thousand troops, opened the granaries and issued rations, and the High Ancestor added to Tai the title General Who Quells Martial Foes.
translations.idiomatic: During Lu Xun's rebellion Tai had already raised a thousand troops, opened the granaries, and distributed provisions; the High Ancestor then gave him the additional title General Who Quells Martial Foes.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷侍中，尋轉度支尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Palace Attendant and soon after made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made palace attendant and soon afterward minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時僕射陳郡謝混，後進知名，高祖嘗從容問混：「泰名輩可以比誰？」

translations.literal: At that time Xie Hun of Chen Commandery, Vice Director of the Secretariat, was a celebrated man of the younger generation; the High Ancestor once asked him at leisure: "To whom among famous men may Tai be compared?"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xie Hun of Chen commandery, a celebrated rising star among the vice directors of the Secretariat, was once asked casually by the High Ancestor, "Among famous men of his generation, whom does Tai resemble?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「王元太一流人也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "He is a man of Wang Yuantai's class."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "He belongs in the same class as Wang Yuantai."

sentences.zh: 徙為太常。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to the post of minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 高祖還彭城，與共登城，泰有足疾，特命乘輿。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor returned to Pengcheng and ascended the walls with him, Tai had an ailment of the foot and was specially ordered to ride in the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor returned to Pengcheng and went up on the city walls with him, Tai, who suffered from a foot ailment, was specially allowed to ride in a carriage.

sentences.zh: 泰好酒，不拘小節，通率任心，雖在公坐，不異私室，高祖甚賞愛之。

translations.literal: Tai was fond of wine, did not bind himself to minor proprieties, and was open and direct, following his heart; even in public audience he was no different from his private chamber, and the High Ancestor greatly prized and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Tai loved wine, cared little for minor etiquette, and was frank and unguarded; even at court he behaved as freely as at home, and the High Ancestor valued and favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 然拙於為治，故不得在政事之官。

translations.literal: Yet he was clumsy at governing, and therefore could not hold offices of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was inept at practical administration, and so was never placed in charge of major policy.

sentences.zh: 遷護軍將軍，以公事免。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Protects the Army and was dismissed on account of public business.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Protects the Army but was later dismissed for an official offense.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，拜金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor received the Mandate, Tai was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor took the throne, Tai was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and given the additional title of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明年，議建國學，以泰領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: The next year, when the establishment of the National University was discussed, Tai was put in charge as Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the court debated founding a national university, Tai was placed in charge as libationer of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 泰上表曰：

translations.literal: Tai submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tai submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞風化興於哲王，教訓表於至世。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that transforming influence rises under sage kings and that instruction and admonition are displayed in the utmost age.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that civilizing influence flourishes under sage rulers and that teaching and moral guidance mark the finest ages.

sentences.zh: 至說莫先講習，甚樂必寄朋來。

translations.literal: In the utmost persuasion nothing comes before lecturing and study; in the greatest joy one must rely on friends to come.
translations.idiomatic: The highest form of persuasion begins with study together, and the deepest joy depends on friends gathering to learn.

sentences.zh: 古人成童入學，易子而教，尋師無遠，負糧忘艱，安親光國，莫不由此。

translations.literal: The ancients, when they reached maturity, entered study; they exchanged sons to teach one another, sought teachers without regard to distance, bore grain on their backs and forgot hardship—all securing their parents and glorifying the state came from this.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients entered school at maturity, exchanged sons for mutual instruction, sought teachers however far away, and carried grain on their backs without minding the hardship; securing one's parents and bringing honor to the state all stemmed from this.

sentences.zh: 若能出不由戶，則斯道莫從。

translations.literal: If one can go forth not by the door, then this Way cannot be followed.
translations.idiomatic: If one cannot even leave home by the proper gate, how can this Way be pursued?

sentences.zh: 是以明詔爰發，已成渙汗，學制既下，遠近遵承。

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened edict has been issued and has already spread abroad like sweat; the regulations for study having been promulgated, far and near comply.
translations.idiomatic: Hence your enlightened edict has gone forth and its influence has already spread far and wide; now that the school regulations have been issued, the realm near and far is ready to obey.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚懷，少有未達。

translations.literal: In your servant's foolish thoughts there are a few points not yet understood.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble understanding, however, a few points remain unclear.

sentences.zh: 今惟新告始，盛業初基，天下改觀，有志景慕。

translations.literal: Now renewal has just been announced and the great enterprise is newly founded; all under Heaven has changed its view, and those with resolve look up in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Your new reign has only just begun and the great enterprise is still being laid; the whole realm is watching with fresh eyes, and men of ambition look to you with admiration.

sentences.zh: 而置生之制，取少停多，開不來之端，非一塗而已。

translations.literal: Yet the regulations for enrolling students take few and detain many, opening avenues by which they do not come—not by one path alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rules for enrolling students admit few and exclude many, opening more than one path by which eager learners are turned away.

sentences.zh: 臣以家推國，則知所聚不多，恐不足以宣大宋之風，弘濟濟之美。

translations.literal: Your servant, extrapolating from the family to the state, knows that those gathered will not be many and fears this will not suffice to spread the wind of great Song or enlarge the beauty of its teeming multitude.
translations.idiomatic: If one judges the state by the household, the number gathered will be small; I fear it will not be enough to spread the civilizing influence of great Song or to display the full splendor of its cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 臣謂合選之家，雖制所未達，父兄欲其入學，理合開通；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that in families qualified for selection, even if the regulations do not yet reach them, when fathers and elder brothers wish them to enter study, reason requires that the way be opened;
translations.idiomatic: I believe that in families eligible for selection, even when the regulations do not yet cover them, if fathers and elder brothers wish their sons to study, the way ought to be opened;

sentences.zh: 雖小違晨昏，所以大弘孝道。

translations.literal: even if they slightly depart from morning and evening attendance, thereby the greater promotion of filial piety is achieved.
translations.idiomatic: even if they must be away from home morning and evening, this would greatly advance the practice of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 不知《春秋》，則所陷或大，故趙盾忠而書弑，許子孝而得罪，以斯為戒，可不懼哉！

translations.literal: Not knowing the Spring and Autumn Annals, the pit one may fall into can be great; thus Zhao Dun was loyal yet the text records regicide, and Xu Zi was filial yet incurred guilt—taking this as a warning, can one not be fearful!
translations.idiomatic: Without knowledge of the Spring and Autumn Annals one may fall into grave error; Zhao Dun was loyal yet was recorded as a regicide, and Xu Zi was filial yet was judged guilty—taking this as a warning, should we not be afraid!

sentences.zh: 十五志學，誠有其文，若年降無幾，而深有志尚者，何必限以一格，而不許其進邪！

translations.literal: At fifteen one sets the will on learning—this truly has its text; if the years are not far below that and one has deep resolve and aspiration, why must one be confined to a single standard and not be allowed to advance!
translations.idiomatic: The canon says that at fifteen one sets one's will on learning; if a youth is only slightly younger and has strong ambition, why confine him to one rigid rule and refuse him entry!

sentences.zh: 揚烏豫《玄》，實在弱齒；

translations.literal: Yang Xiong composed the Profound Meaning while still in tender years;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong drafted the Profound Meaning while still very young;

sentences.zh: 五十學《易》，乃無大過。

translations.literal: to study the Changes at fifty was yet without great fault.
translations.idiomatic: and to study the Changes at fifty was still no great fault.

sentences.zh: 昔中朝助教，亦用二品。

translations.literal: Formerly in the central court the assistant instructor was also drawn from the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the earlier central court the assistant instructor had also been drawn from the second rank.

sentences.zh: 潁川陳載已辟太保掾，而國子取為助教，即太尉淮之弟。

translations.literal: Chen Zai of Yingchuan had already been summoned as staff officer to the Grand Guardian, yet the Imperial Academy took him as assistant instructor—he was the younger brother of Grand Marshal Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zai of Yingchuan had already been recruited as a staff officer to the Grand Guardian, yet the imperial academy appointed him assistant instructor; he was the younger brother of Grand Marshal Huai.

sentences.zh: 所貴在於得才，無繫於定品。

translations.literal: What is prized lies in obtaining talent, not in being bound to fixed rank.
translations.idiomatic: What matters is obtaining talent, not fixing rigid rank.

sentences.zh: 教學不明，獎厲不著，今有職閑而學優者，可以本官領之，門地二品，宜以朝請領助教，既可以甄其名品，斯亦敦學之一隅。

translations.literal: Teaching is not made clear and encouragement is not displayed; now if there are those whose offices are idle and whose learning is superior, they may hold the post concurrently with their original office; for families of the second rank, court gentlemen should be put in charge as assistant instructors—this can both distinguish their standing and is also one corner of promoting study.
translations.idiomatic: Because teaching is not clearly organized and incentives are weak, men who hold idle offices but excel in learning should be allowed to serve concurrently in their present posts; for families of the second rank, court gentlemen should head assistant instructorships—this would distinguish their standing and be one way to encourage learning.

sentences.zh: 其二品才堪，自依舊從事。

translations.literal: Those of the second rank whose talent suffices may continue as before in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the second rank whose talent is adequate may continue in their former duties as before.

sentences.zh: 會今生到有期，而學校未立。

translations.literal: The season for new students to arrive has its term, yet the school has not been established.
translations.idiomatic: The season when new students should arrive is already at hand, yet the school has still not been founded.

sentences.zh: 覆簣實望其速，回轍已淹其遲。

translations.literal: To overturn a basket of earth truly hopes for speed; to turn the wheel back already shows delay.
translations.idiomatic: One who overturns a basket of earth truly hopes for speed, yet to turn the cart around is already to be late.

sentences.zh: 事有似賒而宜急者，殆此之謂。

translations.literal: There are matters that seem to allow delay yet ought to be urgent—this is perhaps what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: There are matters that seem to permit delay yet ought to be rushed—this is surely one of them.

sentences.zh: 古人重寸陰而賤尺璧，其道然也。

translations.literal: The ancients prized an inch of shade and despised a foot of jade—that was their Way.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients valued an inch of time above a foot of jade—that was their principle.

sentences.zh: 時學竟不立。

translations.literal: At that time the school in the end was not established.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the school was never established.

sentences.zh: 時言事者多以錢貨減少，國用不足，欲悉市民銅，更造五銖錢。

translations.literal: At that time those who spoke on affairs mostly said that currency had diminished and state expenditure was insufficient, and wished to buy up all the people's copper and recast five-zhu coins.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many memorialists argued that money was scarce and state revenue insufficient, and proposed buying up all private copper to recast new five-zhu coins.

sentences.zh: 泰又諫曰：

translations.literal: Tai again remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tai remonstrated again, saying:

sentences.zh: 流聞將禁私銅，以充官銅。

translations.literal: It is rumored that private copper will be forbidden in order to fill the state's copper.
translations.idiomatic: I hear it said that private copper is to be banned so that the state's supply may be filled.

sentences.zh: 民雖失器，終於獲直，國用不足，其利實多。

translations.literal: Though the people lose their vessels, in the end they gain compensation; state expenditure is insufficient, and the profit is truly great.
translations.idiomatic: Though the people would lose their utensils, they would finally receive payment; state revenue is short, and the profit would indeed be considerable.

sentences.zh: 臣愚意異，不寧寢默。

translations.literal: Your servant's foolish view differs and cannot rest in silence.
translations.idiomatic: My humble view differs, and I cannot keep silent even in sleep.

sentences.zh: 臣聞治國若烹小鮮，拯敝莫若務本。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that governing a state is like cooking a small fish; to rescue decline nothing surpasses attending to the root.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that governing a state is like cooking a small fish, and that to rescue decline nothing surpasses strengthening the fundamentals.

sentences.zh: 百姓不足，君孰與足。

translations.literal: If the hundred surnames are insufficient, with whom will the ruler be sufficient?
translations.idiomatic: When the common people lack sufficiency, how can the ruler be sufficient?

sentences.zh: 未有民貧而國富，本不足而末有餘者也。

translations.literal: There has never been a state rich while the people are poor, or surplus at the branch when the root is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has a state been rich while its people were poor, or the branches abundant while the root was wanting.

sentences.zh: 故囊漏貯中，識者不吝；

translations.literal: Therefore when the bag leaks into the storehouse, the knowing do not begrudge it;
translations.idiomatic: Hence when the purse leaks into the treasury, the wise do not begrudge the loss;

sentences.zh: 反裘負薪，存毛實難。

translations.literal: to wear the fur inside out while carrying firewood—preserving the hair is in truth difficult.
translations.idiomatic: to wear the fur cloak inside out while carrying firewood—to preserve the hide is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 王者不言有無，諸侯不言多少，食祿之家，不與百姓爭利。

translations.literal: The king does not speak of having or not having; feudal lords do not speak of more or less; families that eat stipends do not contend for profit with the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven does not speak of gain and loss; feudal lords do not haggle over amounts; families on state stipends do not compete with the common people for profit.

sentences.zh: 故拔葵所以明治，織蒲謂之不仁，是以貴賤有章，職分無爽。

translations.literal: Therefore uprooting mallows was how to clarify government; weaving rushes was called inhumane—thus noble and base have their distinctions and offices have their proper allotments without error.
translations.idiomatic: Hence uprooting mallows was held to clarify government, and weaving rushes was deemed inhumane; noble and base each have their place, and offices their proper duties without confusion.

sentences.zh: 今之所憂，在農民尚寡，倉廩未充，轉運無已，資食者眾，家無私積，難以禦荒耳。

translations.literal: What is worrisome now is that farmers are still few, granaries are not full, transport never ceases, those relying on provisions are many, families have no private stores, and it is hard to meet famine.
translations.idiomatic: What we should worry about now is that farmers are still too few, the granaries are not full, transport never ends, too many live on state grain, households have no private reserves, and famine would be hard to withstand.

sentences.zh: 夫貨存貿易，不在少多，昔日之貴，今者之賤，彼此共之，其揆一也。

translations.literal: As for goods, they exist for trade; it lies not in few or many—what was dear yesterday is cheap today; both share in it, and the measure is one.
translations.idiomatic: Goods exist for exchange; the issue is not quantity alone—what was costly yesterday is cheap today, and both sides share the change by the same principle.

sentences.zh: 但令官民均通，則無患不足。

translations.literal: Only let government and people circulate evenly, and there will be no worry of insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: If only government and people circulate money evenly, there will be no fear of shortage.

sentences.zh: 若使必資貨廣以收國用者，則龜貝之屬，自古所行。

translations.literal: If one must rely on broadening goods to collect state revenue, then tortoise shells and cowries and the like have been practiced since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: If the state must enlarge revenue by manipulating currency, tortoise shells and cowries and the like have been used since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 尋銅之為器，在用也博矣。

translations.literal: Considering copper as vessels, their uses are indeed broad.
translations.idiomatic: Consider copper as a material for vessels—its uses are indeed wide-ranging.

sentences.zh: 鍾律所通者遠，機衡所揆者大。

translations.literal: What bells and pitch pipes reach is far; what armillary spheres and steelyard rods measure is great.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and pitch pipes reach far; armillary spheres and steelyard rods measure what is vast.

sentences.zh: 夏鼎負《圖》，實冠眾瑞，晉鐸呈象，亦啟休徵。

translations.literal: The Xia cauldron bore the Chart and truly crowned the multitude of auspices; the Jin bell displayed images and also opened blessed signs.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia tripod bore the Chart and truly crowned all auspicious omens; the Jin bell displayed images and likewise heralded blessed signs.

sentences.zh: 器有要用，則貴賤同資；

translations.literal: When vessels have essential use, then noble and base alike rely on them;
translations.idiomatic: When vessels serve essential purposes, noble and common alike depend on them;

sentences.zh: 物有適宜，則家國共急。

translations.literal: when things have their proper fitness, then family and state share the urgency.
translations.idiomatic: when things suit their proper use, household and state share the same urgent need.

sentences.zh: 今毀必資之器，而為無施之錢，於貨則功不補勞，在用則君民俱困，校之以實，損多益少。

translations.literal: Now to destroy vessels that are necessarily relied upon and make money with no use—in goods the achievement does not repay the labor; in use ruler and people are both distressed; compared in fact, the loss is more and the gain less.
translations.idiomatic: To destroy indispensable vessels and mint useless coin—in trade the effort will not repay the labor, and in daily use ruler and people alike will suffer; judged by fact, the losses outweigh the gains.

sentences.zh: 陛下勞謙終日，無倦庶務，以身率物，勤素成風，而頌聲不作，板、渭不至者，良由基根未固，意在遠略。

translations.literal: Your Majesty toils in humility all day without weariness in the myriad affairs, leads things by your person, and diligence and simplicity have become the wind—yet eulogies are not raised and the songs of Ban and Wei do not arrive; this is truly because the foundation is not yet firm and the intent rests on distant strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty labors humbly all day without tiring of public affairs, leads by personal example, and frugality has become the prevailing custom—yet praise does not arise and the songs of Ban and Wei do not come, truly because the foundations are not yet secure and your mind is set on distant plans.

sentences.zh: 伏願思可久之道，賒欲速之情，弘山海之納，擇芻收之說，則嘉謀日陳，聖慮可廣。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes you to think on the Way that can long endure, defer the feeling that desires speed, enlarge the acceptance of mountains and seas, and choose among straw-gathering proposals—then fine plans will daily be set forth and sagely consideration can be broadened.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to consider what can long endure, set aside the urge for haste, enlarge your acceptance as mountains and seas do, and choose wisely among humble counsel—then good plans will daily be offered and your sage deliberation may broaden.

sentences.zh: 其亡存心，然後苞桑可繋。

translations.literal: Keep the thought of perishing in mind, and then the mulberry on the bank can be tied fast.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the thought of ruin ever in mind, and then the state may be secured as firmly as mulberry roots on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 愚誠一至，用忘寢食。

translations.literal: Foolish sincerity having reached its utmost, your servant forgets sleep and food in presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: My foolish sincerity is complete, and I have forgotten sleep and food in offering this.

sentences.zh: 景平初，加位特進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingping era he was given the special advancement rank.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingping era he was granted the special advancement rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，致仕，解國子祭酒。

translations.literal: The next year he retired from office and relinquished the post of Libationer of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired from office and resigned as libationer of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 少帝在位，多諸愆失，上封事極諫，曰：

translations.literal: While the Young Emperor was on the throne there were many faults; he submitted a sealed memorial of utmost remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: While the young emperor reigned there were many failings; Tai submitted a sealed memorial of stern remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 伏聞陛下時在後園，頗習武備，鼓鞞在宮，聲聞於外；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Your Majesty at times is in the rear garden and rather practices military preparations; drums and shields are in the palace and the sound is heard outside;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Your Majesty often drills in the rear garden, practicing military exercises; drums and shields resound within the palace and are heard outside;

sentences.zh: 黷武掖庭之內，喧嘩省闥之間，不聞將帥之臣，統御之主，非徒不足以威四夷，祗生遠近之怪。

translations.literal: indulging in arms within the inner palaces, clamor between the gates of the secretariat—one does not hear of generals and commanders or lords of command; this is not merely insufficient to awe the four barbarians but only gives rise to wonder near and far.
translations.idiomatic: indulging in arms within the inner palaces and raising clamor at the gates of the secretariat, without the presence of generals or commanders in charge—not only is this insufficient to awe the four quarters, it only breeds wonder near and far.

sentences.zh: 近者東寇紛擾，皆欲伺國瑕隙，今之吳、會，寧過二漢關、河，根本既搖，於何不有。

translations.literal: Recently eastern bandits have been in turmoil, all wishing to watch for gaps in the state; today's Wu and Kuaiji regions—can they be less than the passes and rivers of the two Han dynasties? The root is already shaken—what might not happen?
translations.idiomatic: Recently eastern rebels have been in turmoil, all watching for cracks in the state; today's Wu and Kuaiji regions are no less vital than the passes and rivers of the two Han dynasties—once the root is shaken, what calamity may not follow?

sentences.zh: 如水旱成災，役夫不息，無寇而戒，為費漸多。

translations.literal: When flood and drought become disasters, corvée laborers do not rest, and alarms are raised though there is no enemy—the expense grows ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When floods and droughts strike, corvée labor never ceases, and the realm is put on alert though no enemy threatens—costs mount steadily.

sentences.zh: 河南非復國有，羯虜難以理期，此臣所以用忘寢食，而幹非其位者也。

translations.literal: The lands south of the Yellow River are no longer the state's own; the Jie barbarians cannot be dealt with by ordinary measures—this is why your servant forgets sleep and food and oversteps his proper place in speaking.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland south of the Yellow River is no longer securely ours, and the Jie invaders cannot be managed by ordinary means—this is why I forget sleep and food and speak though it is not my place.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐阼，委政宰臣，實同高宗諒闇之美。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ascended the throne and entrusted government to the chief ministers—this truly matches the beauty of Gaozong's mourning seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne and entrusted affairs to your chief ministers, you have truly matched the virtue of Gaozong who ruled from mourning seclusion.

sentences.zh: 而更親狎小人，不免近習，懼非社稷至計，經世之道。

translations.literal: Yet you draw close to petty men and cannot avoid familiar companions—I fear this is not the supreme plan for the altars of state or the Way of ordering the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you draw too close to petty men and cannot avoid familiar favorites—I fear this is not the best course for the altars of state or for governing the age.

sentences.zh: 王言如絲，其出如綸，下觀而化，疾於影響。

translations.literal: The king's words are like silk, yet when issued they are like cords; those below observe and are transformed, faster than shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's words may be as fine as silk, yet when spoken they bind like great cords; those below look up and are transformed swifter than shadow follows form.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下思弘古道，式遵遺訓，從理無滯，任賢勿疑，如此則天下歸德，宗社惟永。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to think on expanding the ancient Way, model yourself on the legacy teachings, follow reason without obstruction, employ the worthy without doubt—then all under Heaven will turn in virtue and the altars will endure forever.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to reflect on the ancient Way, follow the legacy teachings, act without obstruction where reason leads, and employ the worthy without doubt—then the realm will turn to you in virtue and the altars of state will endure.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「一人有慶，兆民賴之。」

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'When one man has blessing, the myriad people rely on it.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "When one man is blessed, the myriad people rely upon him."

sentences.zh: 天高聽卑，無幽不察，興衰在人，成敗易曉，未有政治在於上而人亂於下者也。

translations.literal: Heaven is high yet hears the low; nothing hidden escapes scrutiny; rise and fall lie in men, success and failure are easy to see—never yet has government been correct above while the people were in disorder below.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is high yet hears the lowly; nothing in the dark escapes its gaze; prosperity and decline depend on men, success and failure are easy to discern—never yet has order reigned above while the people were in chaos below.

sentences.zh: 臣蒙先朝過遇，陛下殊私，實欲盡心竭誠，少報萬分；

translations.literal: Your servant received excessive favor from the former court and special kindness from Your Majesty, and truly wishes to exhaust heart and sincerity to repay even one ten-thousandth;
translations.idiomatic: I received exceptional favor from the former court and special kindness from Your Majesty, and truly wish to give all my heart and loyalty to repay even the smallest part of it;

sentences.zh: 而惛耄已及，百疾互生，便為永違聖顏，無復自盡之路，貪及視息，陳其狂瞽。

translations.literal: but senility has already arrived and a hundred ailments arise together; I must forever part from the sage countenance and have no further path to exhaust myself—greedy still for breath, I set forth my mad blindness.
translations.idiomatic: but senility has overtaken me and ailments multiply; I must soon part forever from your sage countenance and have no further way to serve—yet greedy still for life, I offer this reckless counsel.

sentences.zh: 陛下若能哀其所請，留心覽察，則臣夕殞於地，無恨九泉。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can pity what I request and give heed in reading, then your servant may die this evening upon the ground without regret in the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will pity my plea and give it careful reading, I may die this very evening without regret in the world below.

sentences.zh: 少帝雖不能納，亦不加譴。

translations.literal: Though the Young Emperor could not accept it, he also did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor, though he did not heed the advice, did not punish him either.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之、傅亮等與泰素不平，及廬陵王義真、少帝見害，泰謂所親曰：「吾觀古今多矣，未有受遺顧託，而嗣君見殺，賢王嬰戮者也。」

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and others had long been at odds with Tai; when Prince of Luling Yizhen and the Young Emperor were killed, Tai said to those close to him: 'I have observed much of past and present, yet never seen one who received a deathbed charge and regency, only to have the successor murdered and worthy princes slaughtered.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and others had long disliked Tai; when Prince of Luling Yizhen and the young emperor were killed, Tai told his intimates, "I have read much of past and present, yet never seen one who received a deathbed charge and regency, only to have the heir murdered and worthy princes slaughtered."

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，表賀元正，並陳旱災，曰：

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia he submitted a memorial congratulating the New Year and also reporting the drought disaster, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia he submitted a memorial congratulating the New Year and also describing the drought, saying:

sentences.zh: 元正改律，品物惟新。

translations.literal: At the New Year the calendar is changed and all things are renewed.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year the calendar is renewed and all things are made fresh.

sentences.zh: 陛下藉日新以畜德，仰乾元以履祚，吉祥集室，百福來庭。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, drawing on daily renewal to nurture virtue, looks up to the Qian origin to tread the throne; auspiciousness gathers in the hall and a hundred blessings come to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, drawing on daily renewal to nurture virtue, ascends the throne in accord with Heaven; auspicious signs gather in the hall and a hundred blessings attend the court.

sentences.zh: 頃旱魃為虐，亢陽愆度，通川燥流，異井同竭。

translations.literal: Recently the drought demon has wrought havoc; blazing yang has exceeded its measure; rivers that should flow are dry, and different wells alike are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the drought demon has wrought havoc; the blazing sun has exceeded its proper measure; rivers that should flow run dry, and wells of every kind are exhausted alike.

sentences.zh: 老弱不堪遠汲，貧寡單於負水。

translations.literal: The old and weak cannot bear drawing water from afar; the poor and solitary suffer alone in carrying water.
translations.idiomatic: The old and weak cannot endure hauling water from far away; the poor and isolated struggle alone to carry water.

sentences.zh: 租輸既重，賦稅無降，百姓怨咨。

translations.literal: Rent and tribute are already heavy and taxes are not reduced; the hundred surnames murmur in complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Rent and tribute are already heavy and taxes are not reduced; the common people murmur in complaint.

sentences.zh: 臣年過七十，未見此旱。

translations.literal: Your servant is past seventy and has never seen such drought.
translations.idiomatic: I am past seventy and have never seen drought like this.

sentences.zh: 陰陽並隔，則和氣不交，豈惟凶荒，必生疾疫，其為憂虞，不可備序。

translations.literal: When yin and yang are both blocked, harmonizing qi does not mingle—this is not only famine but surely pestilence will arise; the worries cannot all be listed.
translations.idiomatic: When yin and yang are both blocked, harmonizing qi cannot mingle—not only will famine follow, but pestilence is sure to arise; the worries are beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 雩絜之典，以誠會事，巫祝常祈，罕能有感，上天之譴，不可不察。

translations.literal: The rites of rain-prayer and purification meet affairs through sincerity; shamans and prayer-officers constantly pray, yet rarely is there response—the reprimand of Heaven cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of rain-prayer rely on sincerity in the affair; shamans constantly pray, yet rarely is there any response—the reprimand of Heaven must be examined.

sentences.zh: 漢東海枉殺孝婦，亢旱三年；

translations.literal: In Han, Donghai wrongly killed a filial daughter-in-law and suffered drought for three years;
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Donghai wrongly executed a filial daughter-in-law, and drought lasted three years;

sentences.zh: 及祭其墓，澍雨立降，歲以有年。

translations.literal: when her tomb was sacrificed to, timely rain fell at once and the year had harvest.
translations.idiomatic: when her tomb was sacrificed to, timely rain fell at once and the year brought harvest.

sentences.zh: 是以衛人伐邢，師興而雨。

translations.literal: Therefore when the men of Wei attacked Xing, the army set out and rain came.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the men of Wei attacked Xing, the army marched and rain fell.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下式遵遠猷，思隆高構，推忠恕之愛，矜冤枉之獄，遊心下民之瘼，厝思幽冥之紀。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to model the distant plans, think to elevate the high structure, extend loyal and forgiving love, pity the unjustly imprisoned, let your heart roam among the sufferings of the people below, and set your thoughts on the records of the hidden realm.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to follow far-reaching plans, think to elevate great institutions, extend loyal and forgiving love, pity the unjustly imprisoned, attend to the sufferings of the people below, and reflect on the unseen realm.

sentences.zh: 令謗木豎闕，諫鼓鳴朝，察芻牧之言，總統御之要。

translations.literal: Let the slander-wood be set at the gate and the remonstrance drum sounded at court; examine the words of grass-cutters and herdsmen and gather the essentials of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Let the slander-post stand at the gate and the remonstrance drum sound at court; heed the words of common herdsmen and gather the essentials of rule.

sentences.zh: 如此，則苞桑可繫，危幾無兆。

translations.literal: If so, then the mulberry on the bank can be tied fast and perilous omens will have no sign.
translations.idiomatic: If so, the state may be secured as firmly as mulberry roots on the bank, and perilous omens will find no foothold.

sentences.zh: 斯而災害不消，未之有也。

translations.literal: Then if disasters do not vanish, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Then for disasters not to vanish—there has never been such a thing.

sentences.zh: 故夏禹引百姓之罪，殷湯甘萬方之過，太戊資桑穀以進德，宋景藉熒惑以修善，斯皆因敗以轉成，往事之昭晰也。

translations.literal: Thus Yu of Xia cited the crimes of the hundred surnames, Tang of Yin willingly bore the faults of the myriad regions, Tai Jia relied on mulberry and grain to advance in virtue, and King Jing of Song borrowed the Mars intrusion to cultivate goodness—these all turned defeat into success, as past affairs make clear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yu of Xia took upon himself the people's faults, Tang of Yin willingly bore the myriad regions' errors, Tai Jia used the mulberry-and-grain omen to advance in virtue, and King Jing of Song used the Mars omen to cultivate goodness—all turned misfortune into success, as past events make clear.

sentences.zh: 循末俗者難為風，就正路者易為雅。

translations.literal: Those who follow the decadent custom find it hard to become wind; those who take the correct road find it easy to become elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who follow decadent custom find it hard to set the trend; those who take the correct road find elegance easy.

sentences.zh: 臣疾患日篤，夕不謀朝，會及歲慶，得一聞達，微誠少亮，無恨泉壤，永違聖顏，拜表悲咽。

translations.literal: Your servant's illness grows daily worse; he does not plan for the morrow; meeting the year's celebration he gains one hearing—if his slight sincerity finds a little light, he will have no regret in the springs below, forever parting from the sage countenance; bowing in the memorial he sobs.
translations.idiomatic: My illness grows worse day by day; I do not plan for tomorrow; meeting the year's celebration I gain one hearing—if my slight sincerity finds a little light, I shall have no regret in the grave, forever parting from your sage countenance; I bow in this memorial with sobs.

sentences.zh: 遂輕舟游東陽，任心行止，不關朝廷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took a light boat to travel in Dongyang, following his heart in going and stopping, without regard to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he took a light boat to travel in Dongyang, going and stopping as his heart pleased, without regard to the court.

sentences.zh: 有司劾奏之，太祖不問也。

translations.literal: The responsible office memorialized to impeach him; the Founding Emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office memorialized to impeach him; the Founding Emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 時太祖雖當陽親覽，而羨之等猶秉重權，復上表曰：「伏承廬陵王已複封爵，猶未加贈。

translations.literal: At that time though the Founding Emperor personally held the reins of government, Xianzhi and others still held heavy power; he again submitted a memorial, saying: 'Your servant has heard that the Prince of Luling has already had his title and fief restored, yet posthumous honors have not been added.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, though the Founding Emperor personally governed, Xianzhi and others still held heavy power; Tai again submitted a memorial, saying, "I hear that the Prince of Luling has already had his title and fief restored, yet posthumous honors have not been granted.

sentences.zh: 陛下孝慈天至，友于過隆，伏揆聖心，已自有在。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's filial kindness reaches Heaven; brotherly love exceeds the norm—your servant gauges the sage heart and knows it already has its own intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's filial kindness reaches Heaven and brotherly love exceeds the norm—I gauge your sage heart and know you already have your own intent.

sentences.zh: 但司契以不唱為高，冕旒以因寄成用。

translations.literal: Yet the Keeper of the Tablet takes not speaking as loftiness, and the royal cap strings achieve their use through delegation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Keeper of the Tablet takes silence as loftiness, and the royal cap achieves its use through delegation.

sentences.zh: 臣雖言不足采，誠不亮時，但猥蒙先朝忘醜之眷，復沾廬陵矜顧之末，息晏委質，有兼常款，契闊戎陣，顛狽艱危，厚德無報，授令路絕，此老臣兼不能自已者也。

translations.literal: Your servant's words may be unworthy of adoption and his sincerity may not illuminate the age, but he has rashly received the former court's favor that forgot his ugliness and again been touched by the Prince of Luling's pitying regard at the end; resting in evening he entrusted his substance with more than ordinary bond, sharing hardship in the army camps in danger and distress—thick virtue without repayment, the command at the road's end—this old servant moreover cannot restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: My words may be unworthy and my sincerity may not suit the age, yet I have received the former court's favor that overlooked my faults and again been touched by the Prince of Luling's pity at the end; I entrusted myself to him with more than ordinary bond, sharing hardship in the army camps—great kindness without repayment, the command ended on the road—this old servant moreover cannot restrain himself.

sentences.zh: 朽謝越局，無所逃刑。」

translations.literal: Decrepit and declining, he overstepped his bounds and had nowhere to escape punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: Decrepit and declining, I overstepped my bounds and could not escape punishment."

sentences.zh: 泰諸子禁之，表竟不奏。

translations.literal: Tai's sons forbade it and the memorial in the end was not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's sons forbade it, and the memorial was never submitted.

sentences.zh: 三年，羨之等伏誅，進位侍中、左光祿大夫、國子祭酒，領江夏王師，特進如故。

translations.literal: In the third year Xianzhi and others were executed; he was promoted to Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Libationer of the Imperial Academy, and tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia, with special advancement as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xianzhi and the others were executed; Tai was promoted to palace attendant, left grand master of splendid happiness, libationer of the imperial academy, and tutor to the Prince of Jiangxia, with special advancement as before.

sentences.zh: 上以泰先朝舊臣，恩禮甚重，以有腳疾，起居艱難，宴見之日，特聽乘輿到坐。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Tai was an old minister of the former court and grace and ritual were very heavy, and because he had an ailment of the foot that made rising and sitting difficult, on days of banquet audience specially allowed him to ride in the carriage to his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tai was an old minister of the former court and was treated with exceptional honor, and because a foot ailment made rising and sitting difficult, on days of audience the emperor specially allowed him to ride in a carriage to his seat.

sentences.zh: 累陳時事，上每優容之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly stated affairs of the time and the emperor each time treated him with generous forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly addressed affairs of the day, and the emperor each time treated him with generous forbearance.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，旱蝗，又上表曰：

translations.literal: That autumn there was drought and locusts; he again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: That autumn there was drought and locusts; he again submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 陛下昧旦丕顯，求民之瘼，明斷庶獄，無倦政事，理出群心，澤謠民口，百姓翕然，皆自以為遇其時也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, working from dawn to manifest brightness, seeks the sufferings of the people, clearly decides the many cases, and is untiring in government affairs; reason emerges from the hearts of the multitude and favor spreads in the mouths of the people—the hundred surnames are harmonious, all thinking they have met their time.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rises early to govern, seeks the people's sufferings, clearly decides the many cases, and is untiring in government; reason emerges from the people's hearts and favor spreads on their lips—the common people are harmonious, all believing they have met their time.

sentences.zh: 災變雖小，要有以致之。

translations.literal: Though calamities and changes are small, there must be something that brings them about.
translations.idiomatic: Though calamities and portents are small, there must be something that brings them about.

sentences.zh: 守宰之失，臣所不能究；

translations.literal: The faults of guarding officials your servant cannot investigate;
translations.idiomatic: The faults of local officials I cannot investigate;

sentences.zh: 上天之譴，臣所不敢誣。

translations.literal: the reprimand of Heaven your servant dares not falsely attribute.
translations.idiomatic: the reprimand of Heaven I dare not falsely attribute.

sentences.zh: 有蝗之處，縣官多課民捕之，無益於枯苗，有傷於殺害。

translations.literal: Where there are locusts, county officials mostly compel the people to catch them—this does no good to withered seedlings but harms through killing.
translations.idiomatic: Where locusts appear, county officials mostly compel the people to catch them—this does no good to withered crops but harms through killing.

sentences.zh: 臣聞桑穀時亡，無假斤斧，楚昭仁愛，不絜自瘳，卓茂去無知之蟲，宋均囚有異之虎，蝗生有由，非所宜殺。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when mulberry and grain perished in their season, there was no need for axe and hatchet; King Zhao of Chu's benevolence healed itself without purification; Zhuo Mao removed insects that knew nothing; Song Jun imprisoned the tiger that was strange—locusts arise with cause and ought not to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when mulberry and grain failed in their season, no axe was needed; King Zhao of Chu's benevolence healed without rites; Zhuo Mao removed harmless insects; Song Jun imprisoned a strange tiger—locusts arise with cause and ought not to be killed.

sentences.zh: 石不能言，星不自隕，《春秋》之旨，所宜詳察。

translations.literal: Stones cannot speak, stars do not fall of themselves—the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that one ought to examine this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Stones cannot speak, stars do not fall of themselves—the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that this ought to be examined carefully.

sentences.zh: 禮，婦人有三從之義，而無自專之道；

translations.literal: In ritual, women have the principle of three followings and no way of self-determination;
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, women have the principle of three followings and no way of self-determination;

sentences.zh: 《周書》父子兄弟，罪不相及，女人被宥，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: the Zhou Documents says that among fathers, sons, and brothers crimes do not extend to one another; women receiving pardon has been honored since old.
translations.idiomatic: the Book of Zhou says that among fathers, sons, and brothers crimes do not extend to one another; pardon for women has been honored since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 謝晦婦女，猶在尚方，始貴後賤，物情之所甚苦，匹婦一至，亦能有所感激。

translations.literal: Xie Hui's wife and daughters are still in the palace workshops; first honored then debased—this is what human feeling finds most bitter; a single wife can also be moved to some response.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui's wife and daughters are still in the palace workshops; first honored, then debased—this is what human feeling finds most bitter; even a common wife can be moved to some response.

sentences.zh: 臣於謝氏，不容有情，蒙國重恩，寢處思報，伏度聖心，已當有在。

translations.literal: Your servant toward the Xie family cannot be without feeling; receiving the state's heavy grace, lying down and rising he thinks of repayment—your servant gauges the sage heart and knows it already has its place.
translations.idiomatic: Toward the Xie family I cannot be without feeling; receiving the state's heavy grace, I think of repayment waking and sleeping—I gauge your sage heart and know you already have your intent.

sentences.zh: 禮春夏教《詩》，無一而闕也。

translations.literal: By ritual, spring and summer teach the Odes, and none is omitted.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, spring and summer teach the Odes, and none is omitted.

sentences.zh: 臣近侍坐，聞立學當在入年。

translations.literal: Your servant recently attended at audience and heard that establishing the school should come in the entering year.
translations.idiomatic: I recently attended at audience and heard that establishing the school should come in the entering year.

sentences.zh: 陛下經略粗建，意存民食，入年則農功興，農功興則田里辟，入秋治庠序，入冬集遠生，二塗並行，事不相害。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's strategic planning is roughly established and your intent rests on the people's food; in the entering year agricultural work rises, and when agricultural work rises the fields and hamlets are opened—in autumn one orders the school, in winter one gathers distant students; the two paths proceed together and the affairs do not harm one another.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's strategic planning is roughly established and your intent rests on the people's food; in the entering year agricultural work rises, and when it rises fields and hamlets are opened—in autumn one orders the school, in winter one gathers distant students; the two paths may proceed together without mutual harm.

sentences.zh: 夫事多以淹稽為戒，不遠為患，任臣學官，竟無微績，徒墜天施，無情自處。

translations.literal: Matters mostly take delay and obstruction as warning, not taking distance as harm; your servant as academic official in the end had no slight achievement, only falling short of Heaven's gift and placing himself without feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Matters mostly warn against delay and obstruction, not against distance as harm; yet I as academic official in the end achieved nothing, only falling short of Heaven's gift through my own inaction.

sentences.zh: 臣之區區，不望目睹盛化，竊慕子囊城郢之心，庶免荀偃不瞑之恨。

translations.literal: Your servant's slight aim does not hope to witness the flourishing transformation with his own eyes; he secretly admires Zisang's heart in defending Ying and hopes to avoid Xun Yan's regret of not closing his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: My slight aim does not hope to witness the flourishing transformation with my own eyes; I secretly admire Zisang's heart in defending Ying and hope to avoid Xun Yan's regret of dying with eyes open.

sentences.zh: 臣比陳愚見，便是都無可采，徒煩天聽，愧作反側。

translations.literal: Your servant's recent foolish views were altogether unworthy of adoption, only troubling Heaven's hearing and making shameful restlessness.
translations.idiomatic: My recent foolish views were altogether unworthy of adoption, only troubling your hearing and filling me with shame.

sentences.zh: 書奏，上乃原謝晦婦女。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor thereupon pardoned Xie Hui's wife and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor thereupon pardoned Xie Hui's wife and daughters.

sentences.zh: 時司徒王弘輔政，泰謂弘曰：「天下務廣，而權要難居；

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Education Wang Hong assisted in government; Tai said to Hong: 'Affairs under Heaven are broad, yet holding power is hard to dwell in;
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minister of Education Wang Hong assisted in government; Tai said to Hong, "Affairs under Heaven are broad, yet holding power is hard to sustain;

sentences.zh: 卿兄弟盛滿，當深存降挹。

translations.literal: you and your brothers are full to overflowing—you ought deeply to preserve lowering and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: you and your brothers are full to overflowing—you ought deeply to preserve humility and restraint.

sentences.zh: 彭城王，帝之次弟，宜徵還入朝，共參朝政。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng is the emperor's next younger brother; he should be summoned back to court to join in assisting government.'
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng is the emperor's next younger brother; he should be summoned back to court to share in government."

sentences.zh: 弘納其言。

translations.literal: Hong accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Hong accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 時旱災未已，加以疾疫，泰又上表曰：「頃亢旱歷時，疾疫未已，方之常災，實為過差，古以為王澤不流之徵。

translations.literal: As drought disaster had not yet ended and epidemic was added, Tai again submitted a memorial, saying: 'Recently blazing drought has lasted through the seasons and epidemic has not yet ended; compared with ordinary disasters this is truly excessive—antiquity took this as a sign that the king's favor does not flow.
translations.idiomatic: As drought had not yet ended and epidemic was added, Tai again submitted a memorial, saying, "Recently blazing drought has lasted through the seasons and epidemic has not yet ended; compared with ordinary disasters this is truly excessive—antiquity took this as a sign that the ruler's favor does not flow.

sentences.zh: 陛下昧旦臨朝，無懈治道，躬自菲薄，勞心民庶，以理而言，不應致此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, working from dawn at court without slackening in the Way of rule, personally practices frugality and toils for the people's multitude—by reason one ought not to arrive at this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rises early at court without slackening in governance, personally practices frugality and toils for the people—by reason this ought not to occur.

sentences.zh: 意以為上天之於賢君，正自殷勤無已。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that Heaven toward a worthy ruler is just especially diligent without end.
translations.idiomatic: I think Heaven toward a worthy ruler is especially diligent without end.

sentences.zh: 陛下同規禹、湯引百姓之過，言動於心，道敷自遠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, matching Yu and Tang, cites the faults of the hundred surnames; words move in the heart and the Way spreads from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, matching Yu and Tang, takes upon yourself the people's faults; words move in the heart and the Way spreads from afar.

sentences.zh: 桑穀生朝而殞，熒惑犯心而退，非唯消災弭患，乃所以大啟聖明；

translations.literal: Mulberry and grain grew in the court and perished; Mars invaded the heart and retreated—not only eliminating disaster and quelling harm, but thereby greatly opening sage clarity;
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry and grain grew in the court and perished; Mars invaded the heart and retreated—not only eliminating disaster and quelling harm, but thereby greatly opening sage clarity;

sentences.zh: 靈雨立降，百姓改瞻，應感之來，有同影響。

translations.literal: spirit rain fell at once and the hundred surnames changed their gaze; the response that came was like shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: spirit rain fell at once and the people changed their gaze; the response came like shadow and echo.

sentences.zh: 陛下近當仰推天意，俯察人謀，升平之化，尚存舊典，顧思與不思，行與不行耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought soon to look up and推 push Heaven's intent, look down and examine men's plans—the transformation of peace and ascent still preserves the old canons; it is only a matter of thinking or not thinking, acting or not acting.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty ought soon to look up and follow Heaven's intent and look down to examine human counsel—the transformation of peace and ascent still preserves the old canons; it depends only on whether you will think and act.

sentences.zh: 大宋雖揖讓受終，未積有虞之道，先帝登遐之日，便是道消之初。

translations.literal: Great Song, though it received the end by yielding the throne, has not accumulated the Way of Yu Shun; the day the former emperor ascended to the far journey was just the beginning of the Way's decline.
translations.idiomatic: Great Song, though it received the throne by yielding, has not yet accumulated the Way of Yu and Shun; the day the former emperor died was the beginning of the Way's decline.

sentences.zh: 至乃嗣主被殺，哲藩嬰禍，九服徘徊，有心喪氣，佐命託孤之臣，俄為戎首。

translations.literal: Then the successor was killed and worthy princes suffered execution; the nine domains wandered, hearts grieving and spirits broken; ministers entrusted with the mandate who assisted the orphan soon became leaders of armed strife.
translations.idiomatic: Then the successor was killed and worthy princes were slaughtered; the realm wandered in confusion, hearts grieving and spirits broken; ministers entrusted with the regency soon became leaders of armed strife.

sentences.zh: 天下蕩蕩，王道已淪，自非神英，撥亂反正，則宗社非復宋有。

translations.literal: All under Heaven was in turmoil and the kingly Way was already sunk; unless one were divinely heroic and turned chaos to order, the altars would no longer belong to Song.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven was in turmoil and the kingly Way was already sunk; unless one were divinely heroic and turned chaos to order, the altars would no longer belong to Song.

sentences.zh: 革命之與隨時，其義尤大。

translations.literal: Revolution follows the times—its meaning is especially great.
translations.idiomatic: Revolution follows the times—its meaning is especially great.

sentences.zh: 是以古今異用，循方必壅，大道隱於小成，欲速或未必達。

translations.literal: Therefore ancient and modern use different methods; following the square necessarily blocks; the great Way is hidden in small completion, and desiring speed may not necessarily reach.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore ancient and modern use different methods; following the square path necessarily blocks; the great Way is hidden in small achievements, and desiring speed may not reach the goal.

sentences.zh: 深根固蒂之術，未洽於愚心，是用倡狂妄作而不能緘默者也。

translations.literal: The art of deep roots and firm base has not yet harmonized with your servant's foolish heart—this is why he advocates wild recklessness and cannot keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: The art of deep roots and firm foundations has not yet harmonized with my foolish heart—this is why I advocate bold counsel and cannot keep silent.

sentences.zh: 臣既頑且鄙，不達治宜，加之以篤疾，重之以昏耄，言或非言而復不能無言，陛下錄其一毫之誠，則臣不知厝身之所。」

translations.literal: Your servant is both stubborn and coarse, not penetrating the fitness of rule, and to this is added deep illness and further dim senility—words may be words that ought not to be spoken, yet he cannot be without words; if Your Majesty records even a hair's breadth of his sincerity, then your servant does not know where to place his body.'
translations.idiomatic: I am both stubborn and coarse, not understanding the fitness of rule, and to this is added grave illness and further dim senility—I may speak what ought not to be spoken, yet I cannot be silent; if Your Majesty records even a hair's breadth of my sincerity, I do not know where to place myself."'

sentences.zh: 泰博覽篇籍，好為文章，愛獎後生，孜孜無倦。

translations.literal: Tai broadly read books and records, loved to compose writings, and loved to encourage the younger generation, diligent without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Tai read widely in books and records, loved to write, and loved to encourage younger scholars, diligent without weariness.

sentences.zh: 撰《古今善言》二十四篇及文集，傳於世。

translations.literal: He compiled twenty-four chapters of Fine Words Ancient and Modern and a collected writings, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled twenty-four chapters of Fine Words Ancient and Modern and a collected writings, both transmitted in the world.

sentences.zh: 暮年事佛甚精，於宅西立祗洹精舍。

translations.literal: In his later years he served Buddhism with great devotion and west of his residence established the Jizhi Pure Abode.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he devoted himself deeply to Buddhism and west of his residence established the Jizhi Pure Abode.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 追贈車騎將軍，侍中、特進、王師如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title General of the Chariots of War, with Palace Attendant, special advancement, and royal tutor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was given the title General of the Chariots of War, with palace attendant, special advancement, and royal tutor as before.

sentences.zh: 諡曰宣侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Marquis Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Marquis Xuan.

sentences.zh: 長子昂，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ang died early.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ang died young.

sentences.zh: 次子暠，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His second son Gao was Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Gao was administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 次晏，侍中、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The third, Yan, was Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The third son Yan was palace attendant and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 次曄，太子詹事，謀反伏誅，自有傳。

translations.literal: The fourth, Ye, was Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household; he rebelled and was executed—he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth son Ye was supervisor of the heir apparent's household; he rebelled and was executed—he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 少子廣淵，善屬文，世祖撫軍諮議參軍，領記室，坐曄事從誅。

translations.literal: The youngest son Guangyuan was skilled at composing prose; he was Adviser Staff Officer to the Founding Emperor's son the General Who Pacifies the Army and headed the secretariat office; because of Ye's affair he was executed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Guangyuan was skilled at prose composition; he was an advising staff officer to the Founding Emperor's son the General Who Pacifies the Army and headed the secretariat; because of Ye's affair he was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 王淮之，字元曾，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Huaizhi, courtesy name Yuanceng, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huaizhi, whose courtesy name was Yuanceng, came from Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 高祖彬，尚書僕射。

translations.literal: His founding ancestor Bin was Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His founding ancestor Bin was vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曾祖彪之，尚書令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Biaozhi was Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Biaozhi was minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖臨之，父納之，並御史中丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Linzhi, father Nazhi, and all were Censors-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Linzhi and father Nazhi had both been censors-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 彪之博聞多識，練悉朝儀，自是家世相傳，並諳江左舊事，緘之青箱，世人謂之「王氏青箱學」。

translations.literal: Biaozhi was broadly informed and knew much, skilled in court ritual; from this the family transmitted generation after generation, all versed in the old affairs of the Jiang left, stored in the blue box—men of the age called it the Wang family's Blue Box learning.
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi was broadly learned and skilled in court ritual; from this the family transmitted generation after generation, all versed in the old affairs of the Jiang left, stored in the blue box—men of the age called it the Wang family's Blue Box learning.

sentences.zh: 淮之兼明《禮傳》，贍於文辭。

translations.literal: Huaizhi was also clear in the Ritual Records and ample in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhi was also well versed in the Record of Rites and accomplished in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 起家為本國右常侍，桓玄大將軍行參軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Right Regular Attendant of his native commandery and a traveling staff officer to Huan Xuan, Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as right regular attendant of his native commandery and a traveling staff officer under Huan Xuan, Grand General.

sentences.zh: 玄篡位，以為尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped the throne he was made Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in charge of sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan usurped the throne he was made gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in charge of sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，又為尚書中兵郎，遷參高祖車騎中軍軍事，丹陽丞，中軍太尉主簿，出為山陰令，有能名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi he again became Gentleman of the Ministry of the Army in the Secretariat, was transferred to participate in the military affairs of the High Ancestor's Rapid Cavalry and Central Army, Danyang Assistant Magistrate, chief clerk to the Grand Marshal, went out as Magistrate of Shanyin with a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yixi he again became gentleman of the central army in the Secretariat, was transferred to serve in the military staff of the High Ancestor's rapid cavalry and central army, became assistant magistrate of Danyang and chief clerk to the grand marshal, then went out as magistrate of Shanyin with a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 預討盧循功，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: He shared in the merit of the campaign against Lu Xun and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: For his share in the campaign against Lu Xun he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting.

sentences.zh: 又為高祖鎮西、平北、太尉參軍，尚書左丞，本郡大中正。

translations.literal: He also served as Traveling Staff Officer to the High Ancestor's General Who Pacifies the West, General Who Pacifies the North, and Grand Marshal, as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, and as Senior Evaluator of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as staff officer to the High Ancestor's general who pacifies the west, general who pacifies the north, and grand marshal, as left assistant director of the Secretariat, and as senior evaluator of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋臺建，除御史中丞，為僚友所憚。

translations.literal: When the Song terrace was established he was appointed Censor-in-Chief, and his colleagues feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song regime was established he was appointed censor-in-chief, and his colleagues feared him.

sentences.zh: 淮之父納之、祖臨之、曾祖彪之至淮之，四世居此職。

translations.literal: Huaizhi's father Nazhi, grandfather Linzhi, and great-grandfather Biaozhi down to Huaizhi—four generations held this office.
translations.idiomatic: From Huaizhi's father Nazhi and grandfather Linzhi back through great-grandfather Biaozhi to Huaizhi himself, four generations had held this post.

sentences.zh: 淮之嘗作五言，范泰嘲之曰：「卿唯解彈事耳。」

translations.literal: Huaizhi once composed a five-character poem; Fan Tai mocked him, saying: "You only know how to impeach people."
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhi once wrote a five-character poem; Fan Tai teased him, saying, "All you know is how to impeach people."

sentences.zh: 淮之正色答：「猶差卿世載雄狐。」

translations.literal: Huaizhi answered with a stern face: "Still better than your family's generations of male foxes."
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhi answered gravely: "Still better than your family's generations of male foxes."

sentences.zh: 坐世子右衛率謝靈運殺人不舉，免官。

translations.literal: He was removed from office because, as Censor-in-Chief, he failed to report that Xie Lingyun, Colonel of the Heir Apparent's Right Guard, had committed murder.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because, as censor-in-chief, he had failed to report that Xie Lingyun, colonel of the heir apparent's right guard, had committed murder.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor received the Mandate he was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor received the Mandate he was appointed gentleman at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，奏曰：「鄭玄注《禮》，三年之喪，二十七月而吉，古今學者多謂得禮之宜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu he memorialized, saying: "Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites states that for the three-year mourning, the twenty-seventh month brings auspiciousness; scholars ancient and modern mostly say this accords with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu he submitted a memorial saying, "Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites holds that the three-year mourning period becomes auspicious in the twenty-seventh month; scholars ancient and modern have mostly regarded this as ritually proper.

sentences.zh: 晉初用王肅議，祥禫共月，故二十五月而除，遂以為制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin they followed Wang Su's proposal: the xiang and chan sacrifices fell in the same month, so mourning was ended in the twenty-fifth month, and this became the statute.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jin they adopted Wang Su's proposal, placing the xiang and chan sacrifices in the same month, so mourning ended in the twenty-fifth month and this became law.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，唯晉朝施用；

translations.literal: Since the Jiang left, only the Jin dynasty applied it;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiang left, only the Jin dynasty had applied it;

sentences.zh: 搢紳之士，多遵玄義。

translations.literal: gentry and officials mostly followed Xuan's interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: and gentry and officials mostly followed Xuan's interpretation.

sentences.zh: 夫先王制禮，以大順群心。

translations.literal: The former kings established ritual to accord with the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings established ritual so that it would accord with the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 喪也寧戚，著自前訓。

translations.literal: In mourning, better to express grief—this is recorded in earlier instruction.
translations.idiomatic: "In mourning, better to express grief"—this principle is recorded in earlier instruction.

sentences.zh: 今大宋開泰，品物遂理。

translations.literal: Now the Great Song opens an age of peace, and the myriad things attain their proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Great Song opens an age of peace, and the myriad things have attained their proper order.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜同即物情，以玄義為制，朝野一禮，則家無殊俗。」

translations.literal: I humbly think we should align with present human feeling, take Xuan's interpretation as the statute, and make court and countryside one ritual—then households would have no divergent customs."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe we should align with present human feeling, adopt Xuan's interpretation as law, and unify ritual in court and countryside—then no household would follow a divergent custom."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒左長史，出為始興太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, then went out as Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left chief clerk of the minister of education, then went out as administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，為江夏王義恭撫軍長史、歷陽太守，行州府之任，綏懷得理，軍民便之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia he served as Chief Clerk to the Pacification Army of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and as Administrator of Liyang, exercising the duties of the province and princely establishment; he soothed and embraced with propriety, and soldiers and civilians found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanjia he served as chief clerk to the pacification army of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and as administrator of Liyang, exercising the duties of the province and princely establishment; he governed with soothing propriety, and both soldiers and civilians benefited.

sentences.zh: 尋入為侍中。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered the court as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered court service as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙為都官尚書，改領吏部。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Minister of Justice and then changed to head the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to minister of justice and then reassigned to head the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 性峭急，頗失搢紳之望。
