translations.literal: His nature was harsh and impatient, and he lost much of the gentry's regard.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was harsh and impatient, and he lost much standing among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 出為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 淮之究識舊儀，問無不對，時大將軍彭城王義康錄尚書事，每歎曰：「何須高論玄虛，正得如王淮之兩三人，天下便治矣。」

translations.literal: Huaizhi thoroughly knew old ritual; asked, he had no answer he could not give. At the time the Grand General, Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, was recording affairs of the Secretariat; he would often sigh and say: "Why must one discourse loftily on the abstruse? If one had just two or three men like Wang Huaizhi, the realm would be well governed."
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhi had mastered the old rituals and could answer any question put to him. At the time the grand general, Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, was recording affairs of the Secretariat; he often sighed and said, "Why discourse loftily on the abstruse? Two or three men like Wang Huaizhi would be enough to bring the realm to order."

sentences.zh: 然寡乏風素，不為時流所重。

translations.literal: Yet he was poor in moral bearing and was not highly regarded by the men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lacked moral stature and was not highly regarded by men of the age.

sentences.zh: 撰《儀注》，朝廷至今遵用之。

translations.literal: He compiled Ceremonial Regulations, which the court follows to this day.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Ceremonial Regulations, which the court still follows today.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，時年五十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 追贈太常。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 子興之，征虜主簿。

translations.literal: His son Xingzhi was chief clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xingzhi served as chief clerk to the general who conquers the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，加驍騎將軍、本郡中正，黃門如故，西省職解，復掌宋書。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor received the abdication he was added as General of Agile Cavalry and Senior Evaluator of his native commandery; his yellow-gate post remained as before, his western-office duty was released, and he again took charge of the Song History.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor received the abdication he was additionally appointed general of agile cavalry and senior evaluator of his native commandery; his yellow-gate post remained unchanged, his western-office duty was released, and he again took charge of the Song History.

sentences.zh: 有司奏東冶士朱道民禽三叛士，依例放遣，韶之啟曰：「尚書金部奏事如右，斯誠檢忘一時權制，懼非經國弘本之令典。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized that Zhu Daomin, a smith of the eastern foundry, had captured three rebel soldiers and, by precedent, should be released and sent away; Shaozhi submitted: "The Ministry of Revenue's memorial is as at right; this is indeed a provisional measure for a time of inspection, but I fear it is not a grand statute for governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office reported that Zhu Daomin, a smith at the eastern foundry, had captured three rebel soldiers and, by precedent, should be released; Shaozhi submitted, "The Ministry of Revenue's report is as cited; this may be a provisional measure for a time of inspection, but I fear it is not a lasting statute for governing the state.

sentences.zh: 臣尋舊制，以罪補士，凡有十餘條，雖同異不紊，而輕重實殊。

translations.literal: Your servant has examined the old system: using crime to make up for shortfalls in conscript soldiers—there are more than ten such articles; though they do not differ in kind, their severity in fact differs greatly.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined the old system: using criminals to fill shortfalls in conscript rolls—there are more than ten such articles; though they are of the same kind, their severity in fact differs greatly.

sentences.zh: 至於詐列父母死，誣罔父母淫亂，破義反逆，此四條，實窮亂抵逆，人理必盡。

translations.literal: As for the four articles—falsely reporting parents' death, falsely accusing parents of sexual misconduct, destroying righteousness and rebelling against kin—these four in fact exhaust chaos and defiance; human principle must be utterly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: As for falsely reporting a parent's death, falsely accusing parents of sexual misconduct, destroying righteousness, and rebelling against kin—these four crimes exhaust chaos and defiance and utterly extinguish human decency.

sentences.zh: 雖復殊刑過制，猶不足以塞莫大之罪。

translations.literal: Even if extraordinary punishments exceed the norm, they would still not suffice to block a crime of the utmost enormity.
translations.idiomatic: Even extraordinary punishments beyond the norm would not suffice to answer a crime of the utmost enormity.

sentences.zh: 既獲全首領，大造已隆，寧可復遂拔徒隸，緩帶當年，自同編戶，列齒齊民乎？

translations.literal: Having already obtained preservation of one's head, the great favor is already lofty—how can one again allow them to be pulled out as bondsmen, loosen their belts in the prime of life, and rank themselves with registered households and stand in the same register as the common people?
translations.idiomatic: Having already been spared one's head, the great favor is already ample—how can one again allow them to be drafted as bondsmen, live at ease in their prime, and stand on equal footing with registered households and common people?

sentences.zh: 臣懼此制永行，所虧實大。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that if this system is perpetuated, the harm done will be truly great.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that if this system is perpetuated, the harm will be truly great.

sentences.zh: 方今聖化惟新，崇本棄末，一切之令，宜加詳改。

translations.literal: Now the sage transformation is newly renewed, honoring the root and discarding the branch—all such blanket orders should be examined and revised in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Now that sage transformation is newly renewed and the state honors the root while discarding the branch, every blanket order of this kind ought to be examined and revised in detail.

sentences.zh: 愚謂此四條不合加贖罪之恩。」

translations.literal: I humbly think these four articles should not receive the grace of commutable punishment."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe these four offenses should not receive the grace of commutable punishment."

sentences.zh: 侍中褚淡之同韶之三條，卻宜仍舊。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Chu Danzhi agreed with Shaozhi on three articles but held that the third should remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Chu Danzhi agreed with Shaozhi on three articles but held that the third should remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又駁員外散騎侍郎王實之請假事曰：「伏尋舊制，群臣家有情事，聽並急六十日。

translations.literal: He also rebutted Supernumerary Palace Attendant Wang Shizhi's request for leave, saying: "I have examined the old system: when ministers' families had urgent affairs they were permitted a combined urgent leave of sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: He also rebutted supernumerary palace attendant Wang Shizhi's request for leave, saying, "I have examined the old system: when a minister's family had urgent affairs he was permitted a combined urgent leave of sixty days.

sentences.zh: 太元中改制，年賜假百日。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan period the system was changed: each year one hundred days of leave were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyuan period the system was changed to grant one hundred days of leave per year.

sentences.zh: 又居在千里外，聽並請來年限，合為二百日。

translations.literal: Moreover, those dwelling more than a thousand li away were permitted to combine the years of leave for travel, totaling two hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those dwelling more than a thousand li away were permitted to combine years of leave for travel, totaling two hundred days.

sentences.zh: 此蓋一時之令，非經通之旨。

translations.literal: This was an order for a particular time, not a principle for constant application.
translations.idiomatic: This was an order for a particular time, not a principle meant for constant application.

sentences.zh: 會稽雖途盈千里，未足為難，百日歸休，於事自足。

translations.literal: Kuaiji, though the journey exceeds a thousand li, is not truly difficult; a hundred days' return and rest is fully adequate for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Although the journey to Kuaiji exceeds a thousand li, it is not truly arduous; a hundred days for return and rest is fully adequate.

sentences.zh: 若私理不同，便應自表陳解，豈宜名班朝列，而久淹私門？

translations.literal: If private circumstances differ, one should submit a memorial requesting dismissal—how can one keep one's name on the court roster yet long linger at one's private gate?
translations.idiomatic: If private circumstances differ, one should submit a memorial requesting dismissal—how can one remain on the court roster yet linger at home for long?

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，謂不合開許。

translations.literal: Your servants and I jointly deliberate and hold that permission should not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly deliberate and hold that permission should not be granted.

sentences.zh: 或家在河、洛及嶺、沔、漢者，道阻且長，猶宜別有條品，請付尚書詳為其制。」

translations.literal: Those whose families are in the Yellow River, Luo, Ling, Mian, or Han regions—where the roads are long and arduous—should still have separate provisions; we request that this be referred to the Secretariat for detailed drafting of the system."
translations.idiomatic: Those whose families lie in the Yellow River, Luo, Ling, Mian, or Han regions, where roads are long and arduous, should still have separate provisions; we request that the Secretariat draft detailed regulations."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 坐璽封謬誤，免黃門，事在《謝晦傳》。

translations.literal: He was removed from the yellow gate for a seal-closing error; the matter is in the biography of Xie Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from the yellow gate for a seal-closing error; the matter is recorded in the biography of Xie Hui.

sentences.zh: 荀伯子，潁川潁陰人也。

translations.literal: Xun Bozi was a man of Yingyin in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Bozi came from Yingyin in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖羨，驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xian was General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian was general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父猗，秘書郎。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was a secretary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 伯子少好學，博覽經傳，而通率好為雜戲，遨遊閭里，故以此失清塗。

translations.literal: Bozi from youth loved learning and broadly read the classics and their commentaries, yet he was unceremonious and fond of miscellaneous games, roaming the lanes of his neighborhood—thus he lost the path of clear advancement.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bozi loved learning and read widely in the classics and commentaries, yet he was unceremonious and fond of miscellaneous games, roaming his neighborhood lanes—thus he lost the path of clear advancement.

sentences.zh: 解褐為駙馬都尉，奉朝請，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the sackcloth he became Commandant of the Horse-Enclosure and Attendant at Court, and Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering office he became commandant of the horse-enclosure, attendant at court, and supernumerary palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 著作郎徐廣重其才學，舉伯子及王韶之並為佐郎，助撰晉史及著桓玄等傳。

translations.literal: Compilation Gentleman Xu Guang valued his talent and learning and recommended Bozi and Wang Shaozhi together as assistant gentlemen, helping compile the Jin History and compose biographies of Huan Xuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: Compilation gentleman Xu Guang valued his talent and learning and recommended Bozi and Wang Shaozhi together as assistant gentlemen, helping compile the Jin History and write biographies of Huan Xuan and others.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in charge of sacrifices in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in charge of sacrifices in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 義熙九年，上表曰：「臣聞咎繇亡後，臧文以為深歎；

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen deeply lamented;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen lamented deeply;

sentences.zh: 伯氏奪邑，管仲所以稱仁。

translations.literal: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised its humanity.
translations.idiomatic: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised the act as humane.

sentences.zh: 功高可百世不泯，濫賞無崇朝宜許。

translations.literal: Merit so high may be unextinguished for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Merit so high may endure for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.

sentences.zh: 故太傅鉅平侯祜，明德通賢，宗臣莫二，勳參佐命，功成平吳，而後嗣闕然，烝嘗莫寄。

translations.literal: Thus the late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Huo, was of bright virtue and penetrating worth, second to none among the imperial clans; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was accomplished, yet his later descendants were cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Huo, combined bright virtue with penetrating worth and stood second to none among the imperial clans; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was done, still his later line was cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 漢以蕭何元功，故絕世輒紹。

translations.literal: Han, because of Xiao He's founding merit, whenever the line ended always continued the succession.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Xiao He's founding merit, Han whenever the line ended always continued the succession.

sentences.zh: 愚謂鉅平之封，宜同酇國。

translations.literal: I humbly think the enfeoffment of Juping should be the same as the state of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe the enfeoffment of Juping should be treated like the state of Zan.

sentences.zh: 故太尉廣陵公陳淮，黨翼孫秀，禍加淮南，竊饗大國，因罪為利。

translations.literal: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; disaster fell on Huainan; he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; when disaster struck Huainan he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.

sentences.zh: 值西朝政刑失裁，中興復因而不奪。

translations.literal: It happened that the Western Court's government and punishments lost proper measure, and at the restoration they again followed precedent and did not revoke it.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the Western Court lost proper measure in government and punishments, and at the restoration they again followed precedent without revoking the grant.

sentences.zh: 今王道惟新，豈可不大判臧否？

translations.literal: Now the royal way is newly renewed—how can one not greatly distinguish good from ill?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the royal way is newly renewed, how can one fail to judge good and ill on a grand scale?

sentences.zh: 謂廣陵之國，宜在削除。

translations.literal: I hold that the state of Guangling should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the state of Guangling ought to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 故太保衛瓘，本爵蕭陽縣公，既被橫禍，及進弟秩，始贈蘭陵，又轉江夏。

translations.literal: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; having suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling, then transferred to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan had originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; after he suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling and then transferred to Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 中朝公輔，多非理終，瓘功德不殊，亦無緣獨受偏賞，宜復本封，以正國章。」

translations.literal: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not die natural deaths; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should receive a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to rectify the state's regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not meet a natural end; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should keep a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to set the state's regulations right."

sentences.zh: 詔付門下。

translations.literal: An edict referred it to the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the memorial to the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 前散騎常侍江夏公衛璵上表自陳曰：「臣乃祖故太保瓘，於魏咸熙之中，太祖文皇帝為元輔之日，封蕭陽侯；

translations.literal: The former Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Duke of Jiangxia Wei Yun, submitted a memorial in his own person, saying: "Your servant's founding ancestor, the late Grand Guardian Guan, in the middle of the Wei period of Xianxi, when the founding Emperor Wen was chief minister, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaoyang;
translations.idiomatic: The former supernumerary palace attendant, Duke of Jiangxia Wei Yun, submitted a memorial in his own name, saying, "My founding ancestor, the late Grand Guardian Guan, in the middle of the Wei period of Xianxi, when the founding Emperor Wen was chief minister, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaoyang;

sentences.zh: 大晉受禪，進爵為公。

translations.literal: when the Great Jin received the abdication, his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: After the Great Jin received the abdication, his rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 歷位太保，揔錄朝政。

translations.literal: He successively held the post of Grand Guardian and oversaw recording of court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the post of grand guardian and oversaw the recording of court affairs.

sentences.zh: 於時賈庶人及諸王用事，忌瓘忠節，故楚王瑋矯詔致禍。

translations.literal: At that time the commoner Jia and the various princes held power; jealous of Guan's loyal integrity, Prince Yun of Chu therefore forged an edict and brought disaster upon him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the commoner Jia and the various princes held power; jealous of Guan's loyal integrity, Prince Yun of Chu forged an edict and brought disaster upon him.

sentences.zh: 前朝以瓘秉心忠正，加以伐蜀之勳，故追封蘭陵郡公。

translations.literal: The former court, because Guan held his heart loyal and upright and added the merit of conquering Shu, therefore posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Lanling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The former court, seeing that Guan held his heart loyal and upright and added the merit of conquering Shu, therefore posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Lanling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之中，東海王越食蘭陵，換封江夏，戶邑如舊。

translations.literal: In the middle of the Yongjia period, Prince Yue of Donghai consumed Lanling and exchanged the enfeoffment for Jiangxia, with households and fief unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle of the Yongjia period, Prince Yue of Donghai took Lanling as his sustenance and exchanged the enfeoffment for Jiangxia, with households and fief left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 臣高祖散騎侍郎璪，囗之嫡孫，纂承封爵。

translations.literal: Your servant's founding ancestor the Supernumerary Palace Attendant Sao was Guan's legitimate grandson and inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: My founding ancestor, Supernumerary Palace Attendant Sao, was the legitimate grandson of [text damaged] and inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 中宗元皇帝以曾祖故右衛將軍崇承襲，逮于臣身。

translations.literal: The Central Ancestor, Emperor Yuan, because of his founding ancestor the Right Colonel of the Guard Chong, continued the succession down to your servant's person.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Ancestor, Emperor Yuan, because of his founding ancestor the right colonel of the guard Chong, continued the succession down to my own person.

sentences.zh: 伏聞祠部郎荀伯子表，欲貶降復封蕭陽。

translations.literal: I have heard that Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized, wishing to demote and restore the enfeoffment to Xiaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized, wishing to demote and restore the enfeoffment to Xiaoyang.

sentences.zh: 夫趙氏之忠，寵延累葉，漢祖開封，誓以山河。

translations.literal: The loyalty of the Zhao clan extended favor through successive generations; when the Han founder opened enfeoffments, he swore them with mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's loyalty won favor through successive generations; when the Han founder opened enfeoffments, he bound them with oaths of mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下錄既往之勳，垂罔極之施，乞出臣表，付外參詳。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to record past merit and extend immeasurable favor; I beg that my memorial be taken out and referred outside for joint deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to record past merit and extend boundless favor, and to take my memorial out and refer it outside for joint deliberation."

sentences.zh: 潁川陳茂先亦上表曰：「祠部郎荀伯子表臣七世祖太尉准禍加淮南，不應濫賞。

translations.literal: Chen Maoxian of Yingchuan also submitted a memorial, saying: "Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized that your servant's seventh-generation ancestor the Grand Marshal Huai suffered disaster in Huainan and should not have received a reckless reward.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Maoxian of Yingchuan also submitted a memorial, saying, "Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized that my seventh-generation ancestor the Grand Marshal Huai suffered disaster in Huainan and should not have received a reckless reward.

sentences.zh: 尋先臣以剪除賈謐，封海陵公，事在淮南遇禍之前。

translations.literal: I examine that my founding ancestor, for cutting down Jia Mi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hailing—this occurred before Huainan met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: I find that my founding ancestor, for cutting down Jia Mi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hailing—this occurred before Huainan met with disaster.

sentences.zh: 後廣陵雖在擾攘之際，臣祖乃始蒙殊遇，歷位元、凱。

translations.literal: Later, though Guangling was in a time of turmoil, your servant's grandfather only then received special favor and successively held posts among the foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Later, though Guangling was in a time of turmoil, my grandfather only then received special favor and successively held posts among the foremost.

sentences.zh: 後被遠外，乃作平州，而猶不至除國。

translations.literal: Afterward he was sent far abroad and became governor of Ping Province, yet the state was still not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was sent far abroad and made governor of Ping Province, yet the state was still not abolished.

sentences.zh: 良以先勳深重，百世不泯故也。

translations.literal: Truly because the founding merit was weighty and could not be extinguished for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: This was truly because the founding merit was weighty and could not be extinguished for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 聖明御世，英輔係興，曾無疑議，以為濫賞。

translations.literal: Under sage clarity governing the age, worthy assistants arose in succession; never was there doubt that it was a reckless reward.
translations.idiomatic: Under sage clarity governing the age, worthy assistants arose in succession, and never was there doubt that the grant had been reckless.

sentences.zh: 臣以微弱，未齒人倫，加始勉視息，封爵兼嗣。

translations.literal: Your servant, being slight and weak, has not yet taken his place among men; moreover he has only just barely drawn breath and inherited the enfeoffment by succession.
translations.idiomatic: I, being slight and weak, have not yet taken my place among men; moreover I have only just barely drawn breath and inherited the enfeoffment by succession.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下遠錄舊勳，特垂矜察。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to record the old merit from afar and especially bestow compassionate scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to look back upon the old merit from afar and especially bestow compassionate scrutiny."

sentences.zh: 詔皆付門下，並不施行。

translations.literal: Edicts referred all to the Gate Department, and none was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts referred all memorials to the Gate Department, and none was implemented.

sentences.zh: 伯子為世子征虜功曹，國子博士。

translations.literal: Bozi was Merit Officer to the Heir Apparent's campaign against the barbarians and Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Bozi was merit officer to the heir apparent's campaign against the barbarians and erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 妻弟謝晦薦達之，入為尚書左丞，出補臨川內史。

translations.literal: His wife's younger brother Xie Hui recommended and advanced him; he entered as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and went out to fill the post of Internal Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's younger brother Xie Hui recommended and advanced him; he entered as left assistant director of the Secretariat and went out to serve as internal administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍王弘稱之曰：「沈重不華，有平陽侯之風。」

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Wang Hong praised him, saying: "Solemn without showiness—he has the bearing of Marquis Pingyang."
translations.idiomatic: General of agile cavalry Wang Hong praised him, saying, "Solemn without showiness—he has the bearing of Marquis Pingyang."

sentences.zh: 伯子常自矜廕藉之美，謂弘曰：「天下膏粱，唯使君與下官耳。

translations.literal: Bozi often prided himself on the beauty of his hereditary privilege and said to Hong: "Under Heaven the cream of society are only Your Lordship and your humble servant.
translations.idiomatic: Bozi often prided himself on the beauty of his hereditary privilege and said to Hong, "Under Heaven the cream of society are only you and I.

sentences.zh: 宣明之徒，不足數也。」

translations.literal: Men like Xuanming are not worth counting."
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Xuanming are not worth counting."

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，本邑大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Palace Attendant and Senior Evaluator of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supernumerary palace attendant and senior evaluator of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 又上表曰：「伏見百官位次，陳留王在零陵王上，臣愚竊以為疑。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial, saying: "I have seen the ranking of the hundred officials: the Prince of Chenliu stands above the Prince of Lingling; your servant humbly thinks this doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted a memorial, saying, "I have seen the ranking of the hundred officials: the Prince of Chenliu stands above the Prince of Lingling; I humbly think this doubtful.

sentences.zh: 昔武王克殷，封神農之後於焦，黃帝之後於祝，帝堯之後於薊，帝舜之後於陳，夏後於杞，殷後於宋。

translations.literal: Formerly when King Wu conquered Yin, he enfeoffed the descendant of Shen Nong at Jiao, the descendant of the Yellow Emperor at Zhu, the descendant of Emperor Yao at Ji, the descendant of Emperor Shun at Chen, the descendant of the Xia at Qi, and the descendant of the Yin at Song.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when King Wu conquered Yin, he enfeoffed Shen Nong's descendant at Jiao, the Yellow Emperor's descendant at Zhu, Emperor Yao's descendant at Ji, Emperor Shun's descendant at Chen, the Xia descendant at Qi, and the Yin descendant at Song.

sentences.zh: 杞、陳並為列國，而薊、祝、焦無聞焉。

translations.literal: Qi and Chen both became ranked states, while Ji, Zhu, and Jiao are not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Chen both became ranked states, whereas Ji, Zhu, and Jiao are not heard of.

sentences.zh: 斯則褒崇所承，優於遠代之顯驗也。

translations.literal: This shows that what the enfeoffment honors and upholds is superior to the distant display of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that what the enfeoffment honors and upholds ranks above the distant display of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 是以《春秋》次序諸侯，宋居杞、陳之上。

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals orders the feudal lords with Song above Qi and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals ranks the feudal lords with Song above Qi and Chen.

sentences.zh: 考之近世，事亦有徵。

translations.literal: Examining recent times, there is also evidence for the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Examining recent times, there is also evidence for this.

sentences.zh: 晉泰始元年，詔賜山陽公劉康子弟一人爵關內侯，衛公姬署、宋侯孔紹子一人駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi of Jin, an edict enfeoffed one man of the household of Duke Liu Kang of Shanyang with the rank of Marquis within the Passes, one man of Duke Ji Shu of Wei with Commandant of the Horse-Enclosure, and one man of Marquis Kong Shaozi of Song with Commandant of the Horse-Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taishi of Jin, an edict enfeoffed one man of the household of Duke Liu Kang of Shanyang with the rank of marquis within the passes, one man of Duke Ji Shu of Wei with commandant of the horse-enclosure, and one man of Marquis Kong Shaozi of Song with commandant of the horse-enclosure.

sentences.zh: 又泰始三年，太常上博士劉憙等議，稱衛公署於大晉在三恪之數，應降稱侯。

translations.literal: Again in the third year of Taishi, the Erudites of the Grand Master of Ceremonies, Liu Xi and others, deliberated and stated that Duke Ji Shu of Wei, within the Great Jin, was among the number of the Three Honored, and his title should be lowered to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Again in the third year of Taishi, the erudites of the grand master of ceremonies, Liu Xi and others, deliberated and stated that Duke Ji Shu of Wei, within the Great Jin, was among the Three Honored, and his title should be lowered to marquis.

sentences.zh: 臣以零陵王位宜在陳留之上。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that the rank of the Prince of Lingling should stand above Chenliu."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the rank of the Prince of Lingling should stand above Chenliu."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 遷太子僕，御史中丞，蒞職勤恪，有匪躬之稱；

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, Censor-in-Chief; in office he was diligent and respectful, with a reputation for not sparing his person;
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervisor of the heir apparent's household and censor-in-chief; in office he was diligent and respectful, with a reputation for not sparing himself;

sentences.zh: 立朝正色，外內憚之。

translations.literal: standing in court with upright color, inside and outside feared him.
translations.idiomatic: standing in court with upright bearing, he was feared inside and outside.

sentences.zh: 凡所奏劾，莫不深相謗毀，或延及祖禰，示其切直；

translations.literal: Whatever he memorialized for impeachment, none did he not deeply slander and defame, sometimes extending to ancestors and fathers, to show his severity and directness;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he memorialized for impeachment he deeply slandered and defamed, sometimes extending to ancestors and fathers, to show his severity and directness;

sentences.zh: 又頗雜嘲戲，故世人以此非之。

translations.literal: he also mixed in much mocking play, so men of the age for this reason criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: he also mixed in much mocking play, so men of the age criticized him for this.

sentences.zh: 出補司徒左長史，東陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out to fill the post of Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education and Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as left chief clerk of the minister of education and administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十五年，卒官，時年六十一。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia he died in office, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia he died in office at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 文集傳於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings still circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 子赤松，為尚書左丞，以徐湛之黨，為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: His son Chisong was Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat; because of Xu Tanzhi's faction he was killed by the prime culprit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chisong was left assistant director of the Secretariat; because of Xu Tanzhi's faction he was killed by the prime culprit.

sentences.zh: 伯子族弟昶，字茂祖，與伯子絕服五世。

translations.literal: Bozi's clansman younger cousin Chang, courtesy name Maozu, was five generations removed from Bozi in the mourning grades.
translations.idiomatic: Bozi's clansman younger cousin Chang, whose courtesy name was Maozu, was five generations removed from Bozi in the mourning grades.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，以文義至中書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, through literary accomplishment he reached Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanjia, through literary accomplishment he reached gentleman of the central secretariat.

sentences.zh: 昶子萬秋，字元寶，亦用才學自顯。

translations.literal: Chang's son Wanqiu, courtesy name Yuanbao, also made himself known through talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's son Wanqiu, whose courtesy name was Yuanbao, also made himself known through talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，為晉陵太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Founding Emperor's reign he was Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Founding Emperor's reign he was administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 坐於郡立華林閣，置主書、主衣，下獄免。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned and dismissed for establishing within the commandery a Hualin Pavilion and appointing chief clerks for documents and for robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned and dismissed because, within his commandery, he had established a Hualin Pavilion and appointed chief clerks for documents and for robes.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝末，為御史中丞，卒官。

translations.literal: At the end of the Former Deposed Emperor's reign he was Censor-in-Chief and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Former Deposed Emperor's reign he was censor-in-chief and died in office.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫令問令望，詩人所以作詠；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Fine reputation and fine expectation—the poet therefore composes song;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: A fine reputation and fine expectation are what the poet therefore sings;

sentences.zh: 有禮有法，前謨以之垂美。

translations.literal: having ritual and having law, former deliberations thereby hand down beauty.
translations.idiomatic: to have ritual and to have law is how former deliberations hand down lasting beauty.

sentences.zh: 荀、范、二王，雖以學義自顯，而在朝之譽不弘，蓋由才有餘而智未足也，惜矣哉！

translations.literal: Xun, Fan, and the two Wangs, though they made themselves known through learning and righteousness, yet their reputation in court was not broad—probably because talent was ample but wisdom insufficient; alas!
translations.idiomatic: Xun, Fan, and the two Wangs, though they made themselves known through learning and righteousness, yet won little reputation at court—probably because their talent was ample but their wisdom insufficient. Alas!
